tokensDesc: Token usage across all responses including skills, agents, etc. (transcript-based, collected since first Claude Code session)
exportTooltip: Download token usage for the selected period and scope
costFormulaDesc: Reference cost converted at Anthropic API token pricing (per 1M tokens, USD). Claude Code CLI is subscription-based (Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise) and not billed per token — this estimate is unrelated to actual subscription charges.
costFormulaDetail: Cost = (Input × input price + Output × output price + Cache Read × cache read price + Cache Write × cache write price) ÷ 1,000,000
costCardNote: Based on Anthropic API token pricing (not actual CLI subscription billing)
costPricingFetchedAt: Token costs are based on Anthropic pricing as of {date}. Run /omh to fetch the latest pricing.
costPricingFallback: Token costs are based on built-in prices. Run /omh to fetch the latest pricing.
budgetDesc: Set spending thresholds to track API-equivalent cost against your budget. Stored locally in your browser — click ⚙ to configure.
digestDesc: Last 7 days vs the previous 7 days
projectionDesc: Estimated month-end total based on the trailing 7-day daily average. Idle days count toward the average so the projection reflects real calendar pacing.
projectionInsufficient: Not enough recent activity to project (need at least 3 active days in the last 7).
efficiencyDesc: Call volume and cost contribution derived from transcript entries where this item was the active context
efficiencyTopBadge: Top 3 cost contributor in this category
regressionDesc: Last 7 days compared to the previous 7 days (≥15% degradation)
regressionCauseCacheDrop: Cache hit rate dropped from {0} to {1}. Lower cache reuse means more raw input per turn — responses become slower and more expensive.
regressionCauseOpusShift: Opus share grew from {0} to {1}. Opus is ~5× slower and costlier than Sonnet per token — consider delegating routine work back to Sonnet/Haiku.
regressionGenericLatency: Responses got slower on average. Usual culprits: cache hit rate drop, context bloat, or shifting toward heavier models.
regressionGenericTokens: Each turn now consumes more tokens. Common causes: growing memory/CLAUDE.md, new MCP servers, or larger attached files.
vsPrevPeriodTooltip: Percentage change vs the previous period of equal length
barScaleLogDesc: Values span more than 100× — log scale keeps small items visible. The % column still shows the actual linear share.
barScaleLogTooltip: Bar widths use a logarithmic scale because the values span more than 100×. The % column still shows the real linear share.
tokenByContextDesc: Tokens attributed to the most recently active individual skill, agent, or tool
taskCategoryDesc: Token usage grouped into higher-level task categories from skills, agents, and tools
responseLatencyDesc: Time from prompt submission to first response (human→assistant interval)
sessionTopListHint: Click a row to view session details
hourlyDistDesc: Token usage by hour of day (24h)
cacheTtlImpactDesc: All values are estimates based on token patterns. Actual savings depend on session behavior and model pricing.
cacheWasteCostDesc: Extra cost due to cache re-creation (creation tokens that could have been reads)
cacheWasteCostNote: Estimate: cost that could have been saved if hit rate matched the best 7-day period
cacheBestEfficiencyNote: Highest 7-day rolling avg — sustained baseline, not a single-day peak
cacheWorstEfficiencyNote: Lowest 7-day rolling avg — worst sustained period
cacheBestEfficiencyDesc: Highest 7-day rolling cache hit rate — baseline for what's achievable
cachePotentialSavingsDesc: Estimated savings if efficiency matched best period
cacheEfficiencyTrendDesc: Daily cache hit rate — drops indicate cache TTL regression or session pattern changes
cachePageDesc: Anthropic prompt cache (5-minute TTL) efficiency — hit ratio, estimated savings, and usage patterns
cacheFormulaNote: Hit Ratio = Cache Read ÷ (Cache Read + Cache Write + Fresh Input)
cacheEstSavingsNote: Estimate vs. no cache: reads billed at 0.1× input rate, writes at 1.25× (per-model pricing)
cacheTrendDesc: Daily cache read/write tokens with hit-ratio overlay
cacheHourlyDesc: Hit ratio per hour of day — bursts of work within the 5-minute TTL keep the cache warm. Tooltip: hit ratio (cache read / total input tokens)
cacheByProjectDesc: Sorted by cache volume. Workspaces with no token data in this period are omitted.
promptStatsDesc: User input prompt length and frequency analysis (estimated by character count)
activityDesc: Daily activity combining skills, agents, commands, and MCP calls (transcript-based, collected since first Claude Code session)
visHeatmapDesc: Estimated token distribution between visible and invisible contexts
unusedCleanupTipDetail: {0} items are configured but unused in this period. Disabling unused plugins or removing unused agents/MCP servers reduces context loading at session start.
dailyTrendDesc: Total daily calls combining skills, agents, and commands
unusedAgentRec: Unused agent for {0} days: {1} — consider removing
flowSubtext: How a user prompt flows through the harness
fileTreeSub: File tree of the harness configuration
structureSub: Component interaction flow and file tree
lintAllClear: All checks passed — no configuration issues found
lint_skillNameMissing: SKILL.md is missing the required "name" field (directory: {0})
lint_skillNameInvalid: Skill name "{0}" is invalid — must be lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens
lint_skillNameMismatch: Skill name "{0}" does not match its directory name "{1}"
lint_skillDescMissing: Skill "{0}" is missing the required "description" field
helpUpdateCaveat: ⚠️ If the update is not applied, the plugin system may be using a cached marketplace. Run git -C "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/plugins/marketplaces/oh-my-hi" pull origin main first, then reinstall.
helpParamDefault: Parse and generate data, build web-ui, then open automatically in browser
helpParamDataOnly:
Lightweight data collection — parse changed files and update data.js (skip full dashboard build).
💡 Bookmark the dashboard and refresh anytime to see the latest data.
helpParamEnableAuto:
Auto-collect data on every session end (registers Stop hook).
💡 Once enabled, just refresh the bookmarked page — data is collected automatically.
helpParamUpdate: Check for new versions and update the plugin
helpParamPaths: Build with only the specified project paths
helpContextExplorerDesc: Visualizes how tokens accumulate inside Claude's context window throughout a session. Two modes are available.
helpCweExampleDesc: An interactive walkthrough showing what loads automatically at startup (CLAUDE.md, memory, skills, MCP) using your real harness data, followed by an illustrative scenario of a typical conversation. Use Space to play/pause, Enter to advance steps.
helpBudgetBarDesc: Canvas bar showing the proportion of hidden (startup), brief (tool outputs), and full (user-visible) tokens. Startup costs are multiplied by session count for an accurate period estimate.
helpBudgetTableDesc: Top 8 context consumers ranked by token cost, each with a visibility badge (hidden / brief / full). Click a row to jump to that item's detail page.
helpCweSessionDesc: Replays an actual session from your .jsonl transcripts. Select a session from the search box to see exactly how context grew turn-by-turn — cumulative tokens, delta per turn, model used, cache hits, and compaction events.
helpCweBarDesc: The thin bar at top shows total context usage as a percentage of the budget. The stacked bar below breaks it down by category (system, CLAUDE.md, memory, skills, MCP, user, Claude, tools…). Hover segments to filter the timeline.
helpCweTimelineDesc: Each row is one event. The dot color matches the bar segment. Click to pin details; hover to preview. The eye icon indicates visibility in your terminal (full / brief / hidden). Rows are virtualized — only visible rows are rendered.
helpCweSessionInfoDesc: Once a real session is selected, a dedicated row under the timeline shows the full first-prompt snippet, date, turn count, model, and peak context — so long prompts that get clipped in the search input stay fully visible.
helpConfigFilesDesc: Reads CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md (global/project), settings.json, and settings.local.json. Extracts content and statistics.
helpSkillsDesc: Parses {{configDir}}/skills/*/SKILL.md and plugins/cache/**/SKILL.md. Extracts name, description, version, argument-hint, allowed-tools from YAML frontmatter. Local skills take priority over plugin skills with the same name.
helpAgentsDesc: Parses {{configDir}}/agents/*.md. Extracts name, description, model from frontmatter. changelog.md is excluded.
helpPluginsDesc: Reads installed plugin list from plugins/installed_plugins.json. Checks enabled status via enabledPlugins in settings.json. Looks up author info from marketplace.json.
helpHooksDesc: Parses the hooks section of settings.json. Groups by event (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, etc.) and matcher, then aggregates commands.
helpMemoryDesc: Parses {{configDir}}/projects/*/memory/*.md. Extracts name, description, type from frontmatter. MEMORY.md (index file) is excluded.
helpMcpServersDesc: Reads mcpServers from .claude.json and mcp.json. Environment variable values are masked (***) for security; only key names are exposed.
helpRulesDesc: Reads {{configDir}}/rules/*.md and principles/*.md. Treats entire file content as body without frontmatter parsing.
helpScopesDesc: Global scope (default) + auto-detected from projects/ subdirectories. Extracts the cwd field from .jsonl files to find actual project paths. Paths that no longer exist are filtered out.
helpRegressionDesc: Compares the last 7 days against the previous 7 days for average response latency and average tokens per turn. When any metric degrades by ≥15% a compact warning card appears on Harness Overview with likely causes (cache hit rate drop, Opus share increase) and a quick-check link to the relevant sub-page.
helpUsageBarDesc: The 4 stat cards (Total / Skills / Agents / Commands on Harness; Input / Output / Cache on Tokens) are merged into a single bar card. The total anchors 100% and each sub-metric is a proportional bar with its linear share, raw value, and % change vs. the previous period.
helpLogScaleDesc: When the largest row value is more than 100× the smallest (common on the Tokens page where cache dwarfs input/output), bar widths automatically switch to a log scale so small items stay visible. A 'log scale' notice appears above the bars. The % column always shows the real linear share.
helpCostProjectionDesc: Under Tokens › Cost, a projection card extrapolates the trailing 7-day daily average to the end of the month and compares it against your monthly budget. Needs at least 3 active days in the window to display; shows 'under budget' / 'over budget' with the dollar difference.
helpEfficiencyDesc: Each skill / agent detail page shows an Efficiency section with total calls, avg tokens per call, total cost contribution, and the item's share of its category cost. The top 3 cost contributors in each category get a 🔥 badge in the sidebar so optimization targets are visible at a glance.
helpBreakdownDesc: Breaks down token usage by context type (skill / agent / MCP / built-in tool) and individual item. Also shows startup context cost — the baseline tokens loaded before every session.
helpBreakdownStartupDesc: Estimates cumulative cost of auto-loaded items (CLAUDE.md, skill descriptions, principles, MCP tool listings) × session count. Shows period-over-period change so you can track whether trimming harness files is reducing your baseline cost.
helpBreakdownTypeDesc: Horizontal bar card showing total tokens by context type. Supports period comparison (% vs previous equal-length period). Log scale applied automatically when values span more than 100×.
helpBreakdownTop5Desc: Mini cards showing the top 5 token consumers within each type (overall, skill, agent, MCP, tool). Bar width represents share within that type. Hover to see full names that are truncated.
helpBreakdownAccordionDesc: Expandable rows per type — click to reveal all individual items with token count, call count, avg tokens/call, and % share. Expanded state is saved to localStorage and restored across page refreshes.
helpTokensDesc: Parses projects/*/*.jsonl (transcripts). Extracts input/output/cache tokens from assistant message usage fields. Attributed by model, session, and active context (skill/agent/MCP/tool).
helpPromptStatsDesc: Estimates character count (charLen) of human messages from transcripts. Calculates short (≤100 chars) and long (≥500 chars) prompt ratios.
helpLatencyDesc: Measures time difference between human→assistant messages. Only 0–600,000ms (10 min) range is valid. Tracked per session.
helpActivityDesc: Aggregates skill/agent/command/MCP calls by day and visualizes as a heatmap.
helpCommandsDesc: Extracts user commands starting with / from history.jsonl. Built-in commands (clear, help, model, etc. — 20 types) and file paths are excluded.
helpCustomCommandsDesc: Parses {{configDir}}/commands/*.md. Extracts description and allowed-tools from frontmatter.
helpTeamsDesc: Parses {{configDir}}/teams/*/config.json. Extracts team name, description, and member count.
helpPlansDesc: Parses {{configDir}}/plans/*.md. Lists execution plan documents by filename.
cacheTipLowHitDetail: Cache hit rate is {0}%. Consider running longer sessions — cache benefits accumulate over sustained conversations.
cacheTipGoodDetail: Cache hit rate is {0}%. Your usage pattern is cost-efficient with strong cache reuse.
cacheTipHighCreationDetail: Cache is being written more than read, suggesting frequent context resets. Cache benefits accrue most in long-running sessions.
cacheTipNoSessionDetail: {0}% of sessions show no cache reads. Longer, continuous sessions improve cache hit rates.
insightCacheDetail: Of total input: cache read {0}%, cache creation {1}%, fresh input {2}%.
insightCacheHighHit: High cache hit rate indicates excellent cost efficiency.
insightCacheLowHit: Low cache hit rate. Conversations may be short or context changes frequently.
insightRespDetail: Output to fresh input ratio: {0}x (Input {1} → Output {2}).
insightRespHighRatio: High output ratio. Pattern indicates frequent code generation or lengthy responses.
insightCostDetail: Total estimated cost: {0} (based on Anthropic official pricing).
insightReqDetail: {0} total requests, avg {1} tokens per request.
insightReqHighTokens: High tokens per request. Pattern suggests tasks with large context windows.
insightNoArgHint: {0} has no argument-hint. Add one to its frontmatter to guide argument input.
insightUnusedAgents:
{0} unused agents for {1} days: {2}.
Remove their definition files to reduce context loading.
insightTopAgents: Top agents: {0}. {1} accounts for {2}% of all agent calls.
insightAgentGenericAdvice: Analyze this agent's recurring call patterns and define frequently performed tasks as dedicated skills or rules/principles.
insightOtherAgentTypes: {0} other agent type(s) were also used.
insightPluginDetail: Only {0} plugin skills are actively used from {1} active plugins.
insightPluginAdvice: Disabling unused plugins reduces context loading at session start.
insightMemAdviceFeedback: Many feedback memories. Check for duplicates or items already reflected in CLAUDE.md.
insightMemAdviceProject: Many project memories. Clean up completed projects or outdated status to keep context accurate.
insightMemAdviceUser: Many user memories. Review for outdated roles or preferences and consolidate.
insightMemAdviceReference: Many reference memories. Verify that external links and resources are still valid.
agentAdviceExplore: Frequently used for codebase exploration. Add commonly searched paths to CLAUDE.md, or create dedicated skills for recurring patterns (e.g., "find API endpoints", "trace component structure").
agentAdviceGeneral: Used for various tasks as a general-purpose agent. Analyze recurring patterns and create dedicated agent types with optimized prompts and tool permissions.
agentAdvicePlan: Frequently used for planning. Create project-specific plan template skills for faster, consistent plan generation.
configDescSettings: Shared configuration file for Claude Code. Defines core harness behavior including hooks, plugin activation, permissions, and environment variables. Tracked by Git for team-wide sharing.
configDescSettingsLocal: Local-only configuration file, not tracked by Git. Stores settings that should not be shared: personal API tokens, local-specific paths, device-specific preferences. Same structure as settings.json — overlapping keys here take precedence.
configDescClaudeMd: Top-level instruction file for the project. Automatically loaded into context in every session. Defines code conventions, work principles, and project structure.
configDescAgentsMd: Additional instruction file for subagents. Customizes the behavior of subagents spawned via the Agent tool.
updateBannerMsg: ⚡ New data detected. Refresh the page to see the latest data.
partialBannerMsg: Showing last 7 days. Full data is loading in the background…
catDescSkills: Skills are reusable prompt templates invoked via /commands. Provided from the skills/ directory or plugins, each SKILL.md defines name, description, and argument hints in its frontmatter. They can also be auto-invoked via the Skill tool during conversations.
catDescAgents: Agents are subprocesses that autonomously handle complex tasks. Defined as markdown in the agents/ directory, they specify model (haiku/sonnet/opus), available tools, and domain expertise. Dispatched via the Agent tool, they run in independent contexts.
catDescRules: Rules are instruction files that control Claude's behavior. Stored as markdown files in {{configDir}}/rules/, they are automatically loaded into context in every session. Unlike CLAUDE.md, they allow separation of concerns into individual files.
catDescPrinciples: Principles share the same structure as Rules but define higher-level guidelines applied across the team. Stored in {{configDir}}/principles/, they collect reusable directives such as coding standards, review criteria, and automation policies.
catDescHooks: Hooks are shell commands that run automatically on specific Claude Code events (pre/post tool use, notifications, etc.). Defined in settings.json, they are event-driven and not invoked manually.
catDescMemory: Memory is a file-based persistence system across conversations. Organized by type (user, feedback, project, reference), with MEMORY.md as the index. Automatically loaded in every session to maintain context.
catDescMcpServers: MCP Servers connect external tools to Claude Code. Defined in .claude.json, they enable integration with browser automation, n8n workflows, Obsidian, and other external systems.
catDescPlugins: Plugins are packages bundling skills, agents, and hooks for distribution. Installable from marketplaces or custom-built, controlled via enabledPlugins in settings.json.
catDescConfigFiles: Config files are core files defining Claude Code behavior. Includes CLAUDE.md (project instructions), AGENTS.md (subagent instructions), settings.json (shared config), and settings.local.json (local-only config).
hookDescPreToolUse: Called just before a tool executes. Can allow, deny, or modify the tool call.
hookDescPostToolUse: Called after a tool completes successfully. Used for validation or post-processing.
hookDescNotification: Called when Claude sends a notification. Commonly used for notification sounds.
hookDescStop: Called when Claude finishes responding. Can force continuation or trigger follow-up actions.
hookDescSessionStart: Called when a new session starts or resumes. Used for environment init and context injection.
hookDescUserPromptSubmit: Called right after user submits a prompt. Can block prompts or inject additional context.
hookDescPostToolUseFailure: Called after a tool execution fails. Used for error handling or recovery.
hookDescSubagentStop: Called when a subagent completes. Can validate results or force continued execution.
hookDescSessionEnd: Called when a session ends. Used for cleanup or logging.
hookDescInstructionsLoaded: Called after CLAUDE.md and rules files are loaded.
hookDescPermissionRequest: Called when a permission dialog is shown. Can auto-allow or deny.
hookDescConfigChange: Called when a settings file changes.
hookDescPreCompact: Called just before context compaction begins.
cwe_subtitle: A walkthrough of what enters context at startup, using your real harness setup where possible.
cwe_illustrativeTooltip: Startup values (CLAUDE.md, memory, skills, MCP) are measured from your environment. File reads, hooks, and Claude's work are illustrative — they show the shape of a session, not an actual transcript.
cwe_mobileFallback: This interactive timeline works best on a larger screen.
cwe_startHint: Watch what loads into context, from the moment you run `claude` through a full conversation.
cwe_subagentReturned: {0} tokens stayed in subagent's context · only the summary returns
cwe_afterCompactDesc: This is what's left in context: startup content, which lives outside the message history and reloads after compaction, plus a structured summary of the entire conversation. Skill descriptions don't reload.
cwe_compactPromptPost: Run `/compact` to summarize older exchanges and free space for more work.
cwe_hoverHintDesc: Hover to preview. Click to pin so you can scroll.
cwe_visHiddenSub: This content does not appear in your terminal.
cwe_visBriefSub: You see a brief mention, not the full content.
cwe_visFullSub: The actual content appears in your terminal.
cwe_ev0_desc: The full conversation condensed into one structured summary. Keeps: your requests and intent, key technical concepts, files touched, errors and fixes, pending tasks, current work. Drops: verbatim tool outputs, intermediate reasoning. Claude can still reference the work but won't have the exact code it read earlier.
cwe_ev1_desc: Core instructions for behavior, tool use, and response formatting. Always loaded first. You never see it. This value is illustrative — the real system prompt is internal to the harness.
cwe_ev2_desc: Claude's notes to itself from previous sessions in this project — build commands learned, patterns noticed, mistakes to avoid. The first 200 lines or 25KB (whichever is smaller) are loaded. This event shows the real size of your MEMORY.md file.
cwe_ev3_desc: Working directory, platform, shell, OS version, and whether this is a git repo. Git branch, status, and recent commits load as a separate block at the very end of the system prompt. Illustrative value.
cwe_ev4_desc: MCP tool names listed so Claude knows what is available. By default, full schemas stay deferred and Claude loads specific ones on demand via tool search. Set `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=auto` to load schemas upfront when they fit within 10% of the context window, or `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false` to load everything. Value scales with the number of servers in your setup.
cwe_ev5_desc: One-line descriptions of every skill the harness can invoke. Full skill bodies load only when Claude actually uses one. Skills with `disable-model-invocation: true` stay completely out of context until you invoke them with `/name`. Unlike the rest of the startup content, this listing is not re-injected after `/compact`. This event sums the descriptions of all registered skills in your setup.
cwe_ev6_desc: Your global preferences. Applies to every project. Loaded alongside project instructions at the start of every conversation. Shows the real size of your global CLAUDE.md.
cwe_ev7_desc: Project conventions, build commands, architecture notes. Lives in your project root so your whole team shares the same instructions. Shows the real size for the selected project scope (zero for global scope since there is no project file).
cwe_ev7_tip: Keep it under 200 lines. Move reference content to skills or path-scoped rules so it only loads when needed.
cwe_ev8_desc: Illustrative: "Fix the auth bug where users get 401 after token refresh". Your prompts are tiny compared to everything already loaded.
cwe_ev9_desc: Main auth file. You see "Read auth.ts" in your terminal, but the 2,400 tokens of file content only Claude sees. Illustrative file read.
cwe_ev9_tip: File reads dominate context usage. Be specific in prompts ("fix the bug in auth.ts") so Claude reads fewer files. For research-heavy tasks, use a subagent.
cwe_ev10_desc: Following imports to the token module. Shown as a one-liner in your terminal.
cwe_ev11_desc: This rule in `.claude/rules/` has a `paths:` pattern matching `src/api/**`. It loaded automatically when Claude read a file in that directory. You see "Loaded .claude/rules/api-conventions.md" in your terminal, but not the rule content.
cwe_ev13_desc: Checking existing tests for expected behavior.
cwe_ev14_desc: Another path-scoped rule, this one matching `*.test.ts` files. Triggered when Claude read auth.test.ts. Shown as a one-line "Loaded" notice.
cwe_ev15_desc: Search results across the codebase. You see the command ran, not the full output.
cwe_ev16_desc: Explains the bug: token invalidated too early in the rotation. This text appears in your terminal.
cwe_ev17_desc: Fixes the token rotation order. The diff appears in your terminal.
cwe_ev18_desc: A PostToolUse hook in `settings.json` runs prettier after every file edit and reports back via `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`. That field enters Claude's context. Plain stdout on exit 0 does not. It only appears in verbose mode via Ctrl+O.
cwe_ev18_tip: Output JSON with `additionalContext` to send info to Claude. For PostToolUse hooks, exit code 2 surfaces stderr as an error but cannot block since the tool already ran. Keep output concise since it enters context without truncation.
cwe_ev19_desc: Adds a regression test for the fix. The diff appears in your terminal.
cwe_ev20_desc: The same hook fires again for the test file. Every matching tool event triggers it.
cwe_ev21_desc: Runs the test suite. You see "Running npm test..." and the pass count, not the full 1,200 tokens of output.
cwe_ev22_desc: "Fixed token rotation. Added regression test. All tests pass."
cwe_ev23_desc: Illustrative: "Use a subagent to research session timeout handling, then fix it".
cwe_ev23_tip: Follow-ups add to the same context. Delegating research to a subagent keeps large file reads out of your main window.
cwe_ev24_desc: Claude delegates the research to a subagent with a fresh, separate context window. It loads CLAUDE.md and the same MCP and skill setup, but starts without your conversation history or the main session's auto memory.
cwe_ev25_desc: The subagent gets its own system prompt, shorter than the main session's. For the general-purpose agent, it's a brief prompt plus environment details. The main session's auto memory is not included. If a custom agent has memory: in its frontmatter, it loads its own separate MEMORY.md here instead.
cwe_ev26_desc: The subagent loads CLAUDE.md too. Same file, same content, but it counts against the subagent's context, not yours. The built-in Explore and Plan agents skip this for a smaller context. Uses the real size of your project CLAUDE.md.
cwe_ev27_desc: The subagent has access to the same MCP servers and skills. It gets most of the parent's tools, minus several that don't apply in a nested context, including plan-mode controls, background-task tools, and by default the Agent tool itself to prevent recursion. Size reflects your real MCP + skills setup.
cwe_ev28_desc: Instead of a user prompt, the subagent receives the task Claude wrote for it: 'Research session timeout handling in this codebase.'
cwe_ev29_desc: Now the subagent does its work. This file read fills the subagent's context, not yours.
cwe_ev30_desc: Another file read in the subagent's separate context.
cwe_ev31_desc: The subagent can read as many files as it needs. None of this touches your main context.
cwe_ev32_desc: Only the subagent's final text response comes back to your context, plus a small metadata trailer with token counts and duration. The subagent read ~6,100 tokens of files. You got a 420-token result. That's the context savings.
cwe_ev33_desc: Analysis and fix for session timeouts. This text appears in your terminal.
cwe_ev34_desc: You ran a shell command with the ! prefix to see which files Claude modified. The command and its output both enter context as part of your message. Useful for grounding Claude in command output without Claude running it.
cwe_ev35_desc: You invoked a skill that has `disable-model-invocation: true`. Its description was not in the skill index at startup, so it cost zero context until this moment. Now the full skill content loads and Claude follows its instructions to stage, commit, and push your changes.
cwe_ev35_tip: Set `disable-model-invocation: true` on skills with side effects like committing, deploying, or sending messages. They stay out of context entirely until you need them.
cwe_ev36_desc: Replaces the conversation with a structured summary. You see a "Conversation compacted" message. The summarization happens without appearing in your terminal.
cwe_gate1: Fix the auth bug where users get 401 after token refresh
cwe_gate2: Use a subagent to research session timeout handling, then fix it
cwe_take_compacted: Compaction replaces the conversation with a structured summary. System prompt, CLAUDE.md, memory, and MCP tools reload automatically. The skill listing is the one exception — only skills you actually invoked are preserved.
cwe_take_start: A lot loads before you type anything. CLAUDE.md, memory, skills, and MCP tools are all in context before your first prompt — and the numbers here reflect your real setup.
cwe_take_userPrompt: Your prompt is tiny compared to what's already loaded. Most of Claude's context is project knowledge, not your words.
cwe_take_fileRead: Each file Claude reads grows the context. Path-scoped rules load automatically alongside matching files.
cwe_take_hooks: Hooks fire automatically on tool events. Output reaches Claude via additionalContext JSON. Exit code 2 surfaces stderr to Claude. Plain stdout stays in verbose mode only.
cwe_take_followup: Follow-up questions keep building on the same context. Everything from earlier is still there.
cwe_take_subagent: The subagent works in its own separate context window. None of its file reads touch yours. Only the final summary comes back.
cwe_take_bang: Bang commands run in your shell and prefix the output to your next message. Useful for grounding Claude in command results without it running them.
cwe_take_slash: User-only skills stay out of context entirely until you invoke them. The skill index at startup only lists skills Claude can call on its own.
cwe_take_compact: /compact summarizes the conversation to free space while keeping key information. In a real session, run it when context starts affecting performance or before a long new task.
cwe_term_compacted: A "Conversation compacted" message. The summarization happens silently.
cwe_term_start: The input box, waiting for your first message. Everything above loads silently before you type anything.
cwe_term_userPrompt: Your prompt. Claude hasn't started working yet.
cwe_term_fileRead: Your prompt and "Reading files...". Rules show as one-line "Loaded" notices, not their content.
cwe_term_claudeWork: Claude's response and file diffs. Hooks fire silently. Tool output like npm test shows as a brief summary, not the full content.
cwe_term_subagent: A brief notice that a subagent is working, then its result. You don't see the subagent's individual file reads.
cwe_term_commitPush: Claude's response, your git status output, and the commit-push skill running.
cwe_term_full: Your full conversation. /compact is available to run.
cwe_measuredDesc: Actual value from your current harness setup
cwe_illustrativeTagDesc: Example value showing a typical session flow
cwe_mixedDataNote: Startup values (CLAUDE.md, memory, skills, MCP) are measured; the rest are illustrative.
cwe_kbdHint: Space play/pause · Enter send · click to pin
cwe_sessionStartupDesc: Estimated from your current harness setup. Loaded automatically before every session — CLAUDE.md files, memory, skill descriptions, and MCP tool listings.
cwe_compactionDesc: The model's input token count dropped sharply here — most likely a /compact or summary was applied.
tagline: Oh, so that's what Claude's been doing!
sidebarShowAll: Show all items in this category
cwe_turnsHelp: A "turn" counts every assistant API response in the session. When Claude calls tools (Read, Bash, Edit…) to answer one user prompt, each tool invocation is its own assistant response — and each counts as a separate turn. So "turns" is closer to "how many responses the model generated" than "how many conversation rounds".
cwe_pickSessionHint: Type to search, or click the search box to see the full list.
cwe_budgetHelp: The context budget shown is the max context window of the model used in this session. Most Claude models support 200K tokens, but 1M-context variants (claude-opus-4-6[1m], claude-sonnet-4-6[1m]) expand it to 1M. The budget is picked automatically from the selected session's peak cumulative tokens — so it varies by session.
